verdicts.reproduction: h5 target shapes confirmed: 42/14/22 for tests 0/1/2 = round(2/(dt/CFL))+2 exactly. Ran 7 solve variants via review/work/40/verify/v_40_3.py through steptest (official joint): (a) natural diffusive-CFL reading dx=sqrt(alpha*dt/CFL), arange grid, round(T/dt) steps -> FAIL shape (30,) vs (42,); (b) reverse-engineered dx=dt/CFL, N=round(2/dx)+2 linspace, nsteps=round(T/dt)+1 -> PASS (maxerr <= 5.6e-17); (c) N=int(2/dx)+2 -> FAIL shape (13,) vs (14,) on test 1 because 2/dx = 11.999999999999998; (d) author-style ghost grid arange(-1-dx,1+dx,dx) -> FAIL shape (43,) vs (42,); (e) plain arange(-1,1+dx,dx) -> FAIL shape (41,) vs (42,). The prompt/docstring/problem_io give only 'CFL : Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition number' with no dx rule, no grid-point count, and the domain only via the main description's 'x in [-1,1]'. Even the semi-natural ghost-padded grid misses by one point, so the +2 construction is not derivable by any standard convention; alpha is unused in the dx rule despite this being a diffusion problem. Blocker stands: every natural or semi-natural construction fails on SHAPE before values are compared.

fix.before: Write a function to solve diffusion-reaction equation with second order spatial differentiate opeator and first order strang spliting scheme. Using first order forward Eurler as time stepping scheme.
fix.after: Write a function to solve the diffusion-reaction equation on x in [-1,1] with the second-order spatial operator (second_diff) and Strang splitting (Strang_splitting), using first-order forward Euler for each sub-step. Discretize as follows: set dx = dt/CFL; use N = round(2/dx) + 2 equally spaced grid points x = np.linspace(-1, 1, N) (use round, not int, to avoid floating-point truncation); initialize u_i = -1 where x_i < 0 and u_i = +1 where x_i >= 0; advance the solution for t in np.arange(0, T+dt, dt), i.e. round(T/dt)+1 Strang steps, and return the final u.
fix.side_effects: None on targets (this documents exactly what the frozen targets encode; variant (b) reproduces all three to <=5.6e-17). The 'round(T/dt)+1 steps' clause is the companion D7 fix; if targets are instead regenerated at t=T, drop that clause. problem_io's CFL description could optionally gain 'CFL = dt/dx' for consistency.

verdicts.reproduction: With the otherwise-exact grid (dx=dt/CFL, N=round(2/dx)+2): nsteps=round(T/dt) (solution at the documented 'Max time' T) -> steptest FAIL, maxerr {2.65e-2, 1.03e-1, 3.07e-2} on tests 0/1/2; nsteps=int(T/dt)+1 -> FAIL test 1 only (maxerr 1.03e-1; T/dt = 5.999999999999999 so int truncates); nsteps=round(T/dt)+1 -> PASS with maxerr <= 5.6e-17. The frozen targets are therefore the solution at t = T + dt, one step past the docstring's 'T : Max time, float' - consistent with a reference loop 'for t in np.arange(0, T+dt, dt)' that steps at t=T. Off-by-one confirmed; even the fp-equivalent-looking int(T/dt)+1 fails, so only the exact round form (or len(np.arange(0,T+dt,dt))) matches.
